Welcome to CNC Interactive Learning

A professional desktop application for CNC education

Welcome to CNC Interactive Learning, a professional desktop application designed to teach and practice Computer Numerical Control (CNC) programming and machining workflows. It features an interactive coordinate verification system, a custom G-Code programming environment, and visual schematic inspections.

📥

Download & Installation Guide

Get the latest release and set it up on your system

Get the latest stable release of the application using our permanent, static download link:

Download Link

📥 Download Latest Windows Release (ZIP)
This link always redirects to the most recent release installer.

Step-by-Step Installation Process

  1. Download the ZIP: Click the download link above to download CNC-Interactive-Learning-Latest.zip.
  2. Extract the Archive: Right-click the downloaded ZIP file and select Extract All... to extract the files to a folder of your choice (e.g., your Desktop or Downloads folder).
  3. Run the Installer:
    • Open the extracted folder and locate the installer executable (e.g., CNC Interactive Learning_x.x.x_x64-setup.exe).
    • Double-click the installer to start the setup process.
  4. Follow Setup Prompts:
    • The application installs in Current User mode, meaning it runs in your local user space and does not require administrator privileges.
    • Choose the installation path or leave the default path.
    • Choose whether you want to create a desktop shortcut (recommended for easy access).
    • Click Install to complete the setup.
  5. Launch the App: Once installation is complete, click Finish and open the app from the Start Menu or your desktop shortcut.

System Requirements & Recommendations

Minimum and recommended specifications for running the app

To ensure optimal performance and visibility of technical schematics and editor panels, please review the requirements below:

Component Minimum Requirement Recommended Specification
Operating System Windows 10 (64-bit) Windows 10 or Windows 11 (64-bit)
Display/Screen Size 1280 × 800 resolution 18 inches (18") or larger physical display for an optimum experience
Memory (RAM) 4 GB 8 GB or more
Disk Space 200 MB free space 500 MB free space
Processor Intel Core i3 / AMD Ryzen 3 Intel Core i5 / AMD Ryzen 5 or better
Screen Size Recommendation

The application runs in full-screen mode and renders detailed technical drawings alongside coordinates and G-Code input side-by-side. A screen size of 18 inches or larger is highly recommended to comfortably view all elements without visual crowding.

🧠

State-of-the-Art (SOTA) Practice System

Our automated infinite practice methodology

Unlike traditional CNC teaching methodologies, this application utilizes a complete, automated Infinite Practice System to generate virtually unlimited unique CNC problems:

  • Algorithmic Generated Questions: Automatically creates technical drawings (with proper dimensions), coordinates, and corresponding G-Code using a custom-built Python system.
  • No Repetition / No Copying: Each student gets a unique problem, eliminating answer copying and encouraging actual geometry comprehension.
  • Instant, Detailed Feedback: Evaluates student inputs (both coordinate matrices and G-code execution paths) in real time and highlights mistakes immediately.
  • Industry-Aligned Workflow: Guides students step-by-step through the standard engineering funnel: Coordinates & Dimension Verification → G-Code Programming → Simulation/Machining.
  • Progress Tracking & Difficulty Control: Keeps records of student attempts locally and scales difficulty based on student advancement.

Key Limitations Addressed

The application is designed specifically to solve shortcomings in current CNC training methods:

  • Over-reliance on pen-and-paper practice: Pen-and-paper drafting is fundamentally misaligned with real CNC programming workflows and modern industry practices.
  • Limited practice opportunities: Exercises are typically restricted to only 1–2 static textbook problems per chapter or topic due to manual grading constraints.
  • Rote learning and answer copying: Static questions encourage students to memorize code sequences or copy coordinates without understanding.
  • Delayed and non-specific feedback: Instructors face bottlenecks grading papers, leading to delayed feedback that halts the student's learning cycle.
A First-of-its-Kind Implementation in ITI Training

This approach represents a first-of-its-kind implementation in the ITI training context and reflects a state-of-the-art (SOTA) methodology, combining algorithmic content generation with integrated CNC learning and evaluation. To the best of our knowledge, such a system is not currently in use in ITIs or similar training institutes.

🌟

Core Features

Key functionalities of the learning platform

  • Double-Phase CNC Workflow: Real-world CNC programming workflow. Verify X/Z coordinate points in Phase 1 before moving to G-Code writing in Phase 2.
  • Advanced G-Code Editor: Native line numbers, automated uppercase formatting, syntax highlighting (Pink for codes, Teal for coordinates), and scroll line-snapping to prevent text clipping.
  • Interactive Technical Schematics: Explore engineering drawings by locating and clicking highlighted hotspots to learn component functions.
  • Rich Text-Based Lessons: Instructor-authored rich text guides with embedded images, lists, and reference tables.
  • Local Progress & Attempts History: Work results and quiz history are saved locally on your device and are fully reviewable via the history log.
  • Admin Dashboard: Manage QBank imports, generate tests, upload schematics, structure courses, and view flagged question reports.

Text-Based Lesson

Read instructor-authored educational content with rich formatting

Accessing a Lesson

Lessons appear in your course timeline alongside CNC Practice Activities and Schematic Explorations, identified by a book icon.

  1. Navigate to your course from the Student Dashboard.
  2. Select a chapter containing a lesson activity.
  3. Click the lesson node in the timeline.
  4. The lesson content loads in the main view.

Reading a Lesson

The lesson view presents instructor-authored content in a clean, readable format. Lessons may include:

  • Formatted text — Bold, italic, headings, and paragraphs
  • Lists — Step-by-step instructions and bullet points
  • Embedded images — Diagrams, screenshots, and illustrations
  • Headings — Structured content with H1 through H6 levels

Scroll through the lesson content using your mouse wheel, trackpad, or scrollbar. The lesson content is read-only.

Progress Tracking

StateDescription
Not StartedYou have not opened the lesson yet
In ProgressYou have opened the lesson and are reading
CompletedYou have finished reading the lesson

Progress is marked by the isRead flag. Completed lessons contribute to your overall course completion percentage.

Tip

There is no time limit — take your time reading. Lessons often contain foundational knowledge needed for subsequent activities.

CNC Practice Activity

Two-phase exercise: coordinate input → G-Code programming

Phase 1 — Coordinate Input

Phase 1 — enter X/Z coordinates for each labelled point on the diagram
  1. Study the SVG diagram — each labelled point (P1, P2, P3 …) represents a machining position.
  2. Enter the X and Z values for each point in the table on the right.
  3. All fields must be filled. Empty fields trigger a shake animation.
  4. Click Check / Submit to validate. Correct entries go green ✓, incorrect ones show the right answer.
  5. Your Phase 1 Score is displayed, and the app transitions to Phase 2.

Phase 2 — G-Code Programming

Phase 2 — write CNC G-Code in the Monaco editor

The Monaco code editor (same engine as VS Code) provides syntax highlighting, line numbers, and auto-indentation for G-Code.

  1. Use the editor to write your CNC G-Code program using the coordinates from Phase 1.
  2. Click Run / Simulate to submit.
  3. The system validates your code through multiple passes:
Validation PassWhat's Checked
SyntaxG-Code command format (regex-based)
CoordinatesX and Z within valid machining limits
Feed RatesF values in valid ranges
Spindle SpeedsS values in valid ranges
Tool NumbersT values must be valid

Scoring

If validation passes, your code is compared line-by-line against the expected solution. The Final Score is a weighted combination of Phase 1 + Phase 2 scores. A celebration animation plays on completion! 🎉

Activity Types

TypeHow It Works
FiniteFixed question pool — complete all to finish
InfiniteRandom questions from pool — complete when best score ≥ 60%
Tip

Re-attempting an activity can only improve your score record. Your best score is always preserved.

Supported G-Code Commands

CodeDescription
G00 / G0Rapid positioning
G01 / G1Linear interpolation
G02 / G2Circular interpolation CW
G03 / G3Circular interpolation CCW
G28Return to reference point
G71Stock removal cycle (roughing)
G90Absolute positioning
G92Coordinate system setting
G94Facing cycle
M03Spindle on CW
M05Spindle stop
M08Coolant on
M30Program end and rewind

Scoring Weights

Each question has configurable scoring weights:

ComponentDefault Weight
Phase 1 (Coordinates)50%
Phase 2 (G-Code)50%

Final Total Score = (Phase 1 Score × Phase 1 Weight) + (Phase 2 Score × Phase 2 Weight)

Score Integrity

All scored attempts are cryptographically signed using HMAC-SHA256 by the Rust backend. In your history, each attempt shows an Integrity Status:

StatusMeaning
VerifiedScore signature is valid
InvalidSignature mismatch — possible tampering
UnsignedNo signature (legacy data)

Review Mode

After completing an activity, click Review on the activity node to see your submission in read-only mode — review your coordinates, G-Code, and compare against the expected solution.

Reporting Issues

If you believe a question has an error, you can submit a report. See the Reporting section for details.

Schematic Exploration

Explore annotated diagrams by clicking interactive hotspots

The 3-Panel Layout

┌──────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────┐ │ │ │ │ SVG Schematic Viewer │ Side Panel │ │ (Main Diagram) │ (Info HUD) │ │ │ │ ├──────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────┤ │ Hotspot Grid (Bottom Rail) │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
PanelWhat It Shows
SVG ViewerThe diagram with coloured hotspot circles overlaid
Side PanelLabel + detailed description of the selected hotspot
Hotspot GridColour-coded cards tracking visited vs unvisited hotspots

How to Explore

  1. Click any coloured hotspot circle on the main diagram.
  2. The Side Panel updates to show its label and detailed description.
  3. The bottom grid tracks your progress — visited hotspots light up.
  4. Continue until all hotspots are visited.
  5. Click Finish Exploration to complete the activity (awards 100% score).

Keyboard Navigation

KeyAction
TabMove between hotspot markers
Enter / SpaceSelect the focused hotspot
Arrow KeysNavigate the hotspot grid
EscapeDeselect the current hotspot

You can also pan the diagram by clicking and dragging, and zoom using the mouse scroll wheel.

Note

Progress is auto-saved. If you close and reopen, previously visited hotspots remain marked.

Scientific Calculator

Built-in calculator with trig, memory, and history

Opening the Calculator

Click the Calculator icon in the Global Sidebar to open the calculator panel. Click again to close it.

Operations

CategoryFunctions
StandardAddition, subtraction, multiplication, division
Trigonometricsin, cos, tan (press 2nd for inverse: sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, tan⁻¹)
Power & Rootx², x³, xʸ, √x, ³√x
OtherFactorial (x!), log, ln, π, e
MemoryMC (clear), MR (recall), M+ (add), M- (subtract)

Angle Mode

Toggle between DEG (degrees) and RAD (radians) by clicking the mode indicator in the display area. DEG mode is used for most CNC machining calculations.

Calculation History

Click the History icon in the calculator panel header to view past calculations. Click any entry to recall its result into the current expression. History is preserved across calculator open/close cycles.

Tip

The calculator is available during any activity — use it to calculate coordinates, feed rates, or spindle speeds without leaving the app.

Reporting Questions

Flag issues with questions, activities, or content

When to Report

Submit a report if you encounter:

  • Incorrect answer — The expected coordinates or G-Code appear wrong
  • Unclear question — Instructions or diagram are confusing
  • Missing information — Required data is absent
  • Technical issue — Editor or diagram not working correctly
  • Typographical error — Spelling or formatting mistakes

How to Submit a Report

  1. Open the Side Panel by clicking the sidebar tab.
  2. Select the Report tab (flag icon).
  3. Fill out the form: select a Report Type, optionally specify a Point ID, and write a Description.
  4. Click Submit Report.

Report Status

StatusMeaning
PendingSubmitted, awaiting admin review
ReviewedAdmin has read the report
FixedIssue resolved by admin
RejectedReport dismissed as invalid
Note

Administrators review reports in the Reports tab of the Admin Dashboard. See the Admin Reports section for details.

Course Structure

Build and organise your curriculum: Course → Chapter → Activity

Admin Access Required

All admin features require logging in as Admin. In production, set VITE_ENABLE_ADMIN=true.

Course Structure — create courses, add chapters, link activities

Creating a Course

  1. Type a course name in the Courses input field.
  2. Click the + button to create it.
  3. Click the new course to select it.

Adding Chapters

  1. With a course selected, type a chapter name.
  2. Click + to add. Use ↑/↓ arrows to reorder.

Linking Activities

Select a chapter, then browse the Lessons (schematic) and Exams (CNC) pools on the right. Click + to add any activity to the chapter. Use ↑/↓ to reorder and 🗑️ to remove.

Caution

Deleting a course or chapter permanently removes it and all its links.

🗄️

QBank Manager

Import, browse, flag, and manage the question bank

QBank Manager — import questions, browse by category and difficulty

Importing Questions

  1. Click the Import button.
  2. Select a BankExport JSON file.
  3. Questions are validated, imported, and grouped by category and difficulty (1-5).

Browsing & Flagging

Questions are listed with their QCode, Category, Difficulty Level (colour-coded 1🟢 → 5🔴), and Usage Count. Use the search bar to filter. Click Flag to mark a question for review.

⚡

Test Generator

Create CNC practice activities from the question bank

Test Generator — configure activity name, type, difficulty, and categories

Creating an Activity

  1. Enter an Activity Name in the header.
  2. Toggle Finite / Infinite mode (∞ button).
  3. Choose difficulty mode: Global (uniform) or Custom (per-category via 🌐 button).
  4. Select categories from the left panel and configure levels/counts.
  5. Click ⚡ Generate to create the activity.

Activity Type Details

ModeBehaviour
∞ InfiniteStudents get random questions; complete when best score ≥60%
FiniteFixed pool of questions; all must be completed
🌐 GlobalSame difficulty levels applied to all categories
🎯 CustomDifferent difficulty levels per category
🎨

Asset Pool (Schematics)

Upload diagram images and hotspot JSON to create schematic activities

Asset Pool — upload images and JSON, preview schematic activities

Creating a Schematic

  1. Enter a Schematic Name.
  2. Click Upload Image — select a PNG, JPG, or SVG file.
  3. Click Upload JSON — select the hotspot definition file.
  4. Click Create Schematic to save.

Hotspot JSON Format

[
  {
    "id": "hotspot-1",
    "x": 150,
    "y": 220,
    "radius": 20,
    "label": "Chuck Jaw",
    "detailedDescription": "Holds the workpiece..."
  }
]

Creating a Text-Based Lesson

  1. Toggle the interface to Text Lesson Mode.
  2. Enter a Lesson Title.
  3. Use the integrated TipTap Rich Text Editor to write the lesson content — format text, create lists, add headings, and drag-and-drop images.
  4. Click Save Lesson to add it to the asset pool.

Glossary

Key terms used throughout the application

TermDefinition
ActivityA single learning exercise — CNC practice, schematic exploration, or text lesson
ChapterA group of related activities within a course
CourseThe full learning programme, made up of sequential chapters
Finite ActivityFixed question pool — every question must be completed
Infinite ActivityRandom questions from pool — complete when best score ≥ 60%
G-CodeThe programming language used to control CNC machine tools
HotspotAn interactive clickable point overlaid on a schematic diagram
QCodeUnique identifier for each question in the question bank
QBankQuestion Bank — the central repository of all CNC questions
BankExportThe JSON file format used to import questions into the QBank
Text LessonRich text content created using the integrated TipTap editor
ReportA student-submitted issue flag for admin review
CalculatorBuilt-in scientific calculator with trig, memory, and history
Integrity StatusScore verification status: verified, invalid, unsigned, or pending
